task_message:
Case N07: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 181x181x100 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. 

**Summary for N07 (peripheral nerve sheath tumor, T2 MRI):**
- **Lesion found:** a large, heterogeneous hyperintense mass in the lateral subcutaneous/soft tissue of the limb (patient right), spanning ~48 mm (lateral) × ~67 mm (AP) × ~48 mm cranio-caudal, with a bright lobulated periphery and darker central/necrotic regions.
- **Segmentation approach:** located it on multi-plane contact sheets, then seeded it with a positive lasso on the axial slice through the largest cross-section. The initial model output included small vessel/fascia leak components, which I removed with a `keep_component` edit; a model refinement then produced the final mask (v3, 64.0 mL, single connected component).
- **Verification:** checked the mask on the axial, coronal and sagittal ends (including past-the-end slices, which showed no residual lesion tissue), verified the boundary follows the bright mass on all three planes, and rejected all four automatic candidates (C1–C4) as adjacent fat/vessel rather than tumor.
- **Confidence: medium** — the outline tracks the lesion boundary well in all three planes; the only residual uncertainty is the bright periphery, where surrounding fat is also hyperintense on T2.
